claude.sample_unit: pediatric conditions and symptoms (36 ChatGPT explanations each)

links.outcome: Whether generated materials reached requested reading grade levels at baseline and after output selection
links.effect: Few prompts reached requested RGLs at baseline. After selection, median RGLs were 5.8 (level 1), 7.5 (level 2), 9.5 (level 3), and 11.5 (level 4).
links.quote: Prompt architectures varied in how well they initially resulted in a desired RGL, and few prompts resulted in requested RGLs at baseline.

links.outcome: Proportion of AI outputs needing expert accuracy and completeness edits
links.effect: 93.5%, 95.5%, 95.5%, and 95.0% of outputs for levels 1 to 4 needed no word additions or deletions, so about 4.5-6.5% needed edits.
links.quote: Accuracy edits were minimal, with 93.5%, 95.5%, 95.5%, and 95.0% of outputs requiring no word additions or deletions for levels 1 through 4, respectively.

unlisted_practices: Generating many LLM outputs per topic and selecting the one closest to the target reading grade level, rather than relying on prompt instructions alone

links.effect: After selection and accuracy edits, median RGLs were 5.8, 7.5, 9.5, and 11.5 for levels 1 through 4.
links.quote: After output selection and accuracy edits, median RGLs were 5.8 (5.4-6.4) for level 1, 7.5 (7.4-7.7) for level 2, 9.5 (9.4-9.7) for level 3, and 11.5 (11.3-11.7) for level 4.

links.effect: 93.5%, 95.5%, 95.5%, and 95.0% of outputs required no word additions or deletions for levels 1 through 4.

screen.practice: reading-level constraints with output selection and expert review
screen.reason: The study tests prompt design and output selection constraints based on reading grade levels (RGLs) combined with expert clinician review to ensure pediatric patient health information reaches target readability levels safely.
